newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end quiet, focus remains on ITC.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end quiet, focus remains on ITC.

text.p: ** (1230 GMT) - Profit taking brakes early rally in Indian
shares close on profit-taking, focus on ITC ahead of
results on Tuesday
** Bombay share index up 18.67 points, or 0.50 pct at
3,778.31, off intra-day high 3,806.15
** ITC stock ends 6.50 rupees up at 448.50, analysts expect
sharply higher profit for fiscal 1996/97
** Bajaj Auto sets one-for-two bonus share issue, stock
down 4.75 rupees at 866.0
** National exchange 50-stock index closes 2.40 points
higher at 1,050.80 provisional
Indian tobacco conglomerate ITC Ltd was in the limelight at Bombay exchanges on Monday but other shares ended flat as profit-taking wiped out a sharp early rally, traders said.
"We saw some profit-taking in small cap stocks today, but the markets were led by ITC," said Maulik Sharedalal, a member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange.
ITC is expected to report sharply higher profits for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) on the back of robust growth in cigarette sales and improved margins, analysts said on Monday.
The results are due on Tuesday.
Traders said the market was likely to stay in a small trading band as investors book profits at higher levels.
They said investors have become more selective, focussing on bargain-priced stocks after a spate of company results showed the effects of an economic slowdown and tighter margins.
"Sectors that can be bought at current levels are software and pharmaceuticals," said Girish Desai, head of reseach at Prabhudas Lilladher Pvt Ltd.
The Calcutta share index rose 0.22 points to end at 107.32 and the Madras index 25.59 points to 3,626.05.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
